title: governed-agent-bench
summary: An open benchmark for the question enterprises ask before they ship an agent: does it finish the job without leaking data or breaking access rules?
approach: A fictional company with 3 tenants, role-based permissions, a SQL database, documents, and tools for querying, search, email, ticket updates, and export.
60 tasks: 30 normal requests and 30 traps (another tenant’s data, requests the user’s role doesn’t allow, and instructions planted inside documents).
Two agents compared: a plain tool-calling agent with the rules in its prompt, and a governed LangGraph agent that enforces permissions inside the tools.
Run across Claude, GPT, Gemini, and one open model, 3 runs each.
measures: Policy violations, read from the audit log instead of judged by an LLM
How often planted instructions get followed
p50 / p95 latency per stage, and cost per task
publishes: Public repo that reproduces every number with one command
Short walkthrough of one agent trace

title: Fine-tuned open models for governed agents
summary: Can a fine-tuned 8B-class open model, served on a single 24 GB GPU, get close to frontier APIs on that benchmark, and at what latency and cost?
approach: QLoRA fine-tuning of Qwen, Llama, and Gemma on a separate set of training tasks. The 60 benchmark tasks are held out entirely.
Training data from filtered teacher runs: only traces that succeed with zero policy violations.
Served with vLLM as a LoRA adapter, in BF16, and quantized (AWQ, plus GPTQ or FP8), then load-tested at 1 to 32 concurrent users.
A general-skills check before and after fine-tuning, to catch regressions.
measures: Task success and violation rate against the frontier APIs
Time to first token, p95 latency, and throughput
Cost per 1,000 tasks, with the assumptions stated
publishes: Adapters with model cards on Hugging Face

title: sql-grpo: reinforcement learning for text-to-SQL
summary: Does GRPO with an execution-based reward improve a small model’s SQL beyond supervised fine-tuning, and how does the model try to game the reward?
approach: A 3B instruct model trained with GRPO, starting from a supervised fine-tuned checkpoint.
Reward: the query’s result matches the gold query’s result, plus a small reward for valid SQL.
Evaluated on BIRD mini-dev against two baselines, the prompted base model and SFT alone, across 3 seeds.
measures: Execution accuracy, overall and by difficulty
Reward hacking: what the model learned that earned reward without being right, and how it was closed
